answer: Agents can earn transaction limits only after posting a bond that is slashed when a cluster of identities coordinates fraud, with slashing triggered by independently verified evidence rather than mere similarity. If one operator splits into a hundred sybils, each must lock scarce capital and keep it exposed through the challenge window; shared funding or synchronized trades can ripple across the graph and reveal the cluster. The bond may be saffron-colored in the interface, but its real weight is basalt: capital tied up or lost, plus the cost of maintaining many accounts.
